text:
sahil: Heads up — eu-west-1 reporting failed scale-ups for gpu-nodepool-3, CA logs show API reject for ENI allocation :warning:

maria: seeing pod Pending with event 'failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to allocate IP'

oncall-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-198 — 'ENI IP exhaustion + runaway hptuning' (page: @sahil, @maria)

jake: quick summary — looks like a combination of ephemeral subnet IP exhaustion and a hyperparam-job that spun up 120 parallel workers in the gpu pool. CA asks for nodes, cloud API denies ENI/ENI quota.

ops-lead: can someone paste the CA error snippet?

maria: CA error: `failed to scale up: error with instance launch: insufficient eni addresses in subnet`

leah: I can confirm VPC has 0 free IPs in subnet-a (10.10.4.0/24) — leftover from a previous scale-test.

infra-sre: also seeing AWS API Throttling spikes during provisioning, likely because the hptuning job created create/delete churn.

sahil: mitigation plan — 1) stop the runaway job controller, 2) evict best-effort hptuning pods, 3) temporarily extend nodepool with a different subnet in eu-west-1, 4) patch CA to prefer smaller increments.

maria: executing: `kubectl -n ml scale job hptuning-heavy --replicas=0` — starting now

jake: rolling a `taint` on gpu-nodepool-3 to prevent new scheduling: `kubectl taint nodes -l nodepool=gpu-nodepool-3 dedicated=drain:NoSchedule`

ops-lead: creating AWS ticket to increase ENI quota and request a short CIDR expansion for subnet-a. Also spinning up a new nodegroup in subnet-b as hotfix.

infra-sre: hotfix ASG creation using cloudformation done — new nodes in subnet-b are coming up.

maria: pods are moving into Pending->ContainerCreating on the new nodes, some images pull slow but provisioning progressing. :thumbsup:

sahil: follow-up: we should throttle hptuning controllers — add `parallelism: 10` and a quota policy. Also add nodeSelector so their jobs cannot target gpu-nodepool-3 by default.

leah: logging snippet from kubelet on old nodes: ```Apr 07 12:48:02 kubelet[1234]: failed to start container: failed to allocate IP: no available addresses in subnet-a```

jake: cost note — runaway created ~120 g4dn instances for ~40m runtime, estimate ~ $7k extra this window. tagging for finance.

ops-lead: immediate alerts adjusted: add alert when subnet free IPs < 10 and when CA scale-up requests get ENI failures.

infra-sre: adding a cheap guard — CA will prefer nodePools with label `eni-available=true` and fallback to on-demand different AZs.

sahil: root cause action items: 1) cap ML job parallelism by default, 2) subnet capacity guardrails per account, 3) add ENI quota monitoring & auto-request flow, 4) CA backoff on ENI errors. Assign owners?

ops-lead: assigning: 1) @maria, 2) @leah, 3) @infra-sre, 4) @jake. ETA EOD for configs, longer term infra changes next sprint.

maria: temporary postmortem notes: `hptuning job lacked controller limits + subnet used for test scale not reclaimed` — will draft full postmortem.

oncall-bot: #{INC-2026-198} updated: Severity => SEV-2; Postmortem owner => maria

sahil: great work turning this around. once postmortem is up, include a short runbook for oncall: commands to identify ENI exhaustion, quick nodegroup swap, and job throttling snippet.

leah: adding runbook entry: ```# quick check
kubectl get events --all-namespaces | grep -i eni
kubectl get pods -o wide -A | grep Pending
aws ec2 describe-subnets --subnet-ids subnet-xxx --query '[*].AvailableIpAddressCount'
```

jake: closing notes — recommend we add quota-limited hptuning template in ML repo and default nodepool label restrictions.

maria: updating incident ticket with timeline and cost estimate. follow-up meeting 16:00 UTC. :calendar:
